title: Implementation-Leaked Naming
pattern: Variables, fields, structs, or functions are named after their low-level implementation details rather than their functional, domain-level role.
why_bad: It leaks details of the implementation to readers and users. If the underlying data structure changes from a `Vec` to a `HashMap`, or the database switches from SQL to a NoSQL store, the names become misleading or force widespread renames.
detection: Names containing container types (e.g., `_vector`, `_list`, `_hashmap`) or specific database/framework technologies (e.g., `sql_`, `redis_`) inside high-level business layers.
counterexample: Low-level drivers or system utilities where referencing the exact technology in the name is essential for clarity.
fix: Rename variables and functions functionally for what they represent in the domain (e.g., `users` instead of `user_vector`, `find_user` instead of `query_from_sql_db`).
source: Robert C. Martin, *Clean Code* (2008), Chapter 17, G6 ("Names at the appropriate level of abstraction"); Steve McConnell, *Code Complete* (2004), Chapter 11.
